Let \(s=1/q\). Since \(q^3-3q^2-1=0\), we have

\[
1-3s-s^3=0.
\]

First extract the \(z\)-coefficient:

\[
F(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{1-x-y-z(1+xy)},
\]

so

\[
[z^n]F(x,y,z)=\frac{(1+xy)^n}{(1-x-y)^{n+1}}.
\]

Thus

\[
a_n=[x^ny^n]\frac{(1+xy)^n}{(1-x-y)^{n+1}}.
\]

Use Cauchy’s formula on \(|x|=|y|=s\), writing \(x=se^{i\theta}\), \(y=se^{i\phi}\). Then

\[
a_n=\frac1{(2\pi)^2}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
\left(
\frac{1+s^2e^{i(\theta+\phi)}}{s^2e^{i(\theta+\phi)}(1-se^{i\theta}-se^{i\phi})}
\right)^n
\frac{d\theta\,d\phi}{1-se^{i\theta}-se^{i\phi}}.
\]

At \((0,0)\), the exponential base equals

\[
\frac{1+s^2}{s^2(1-2s)}.
\]

Using \(1-3s-s^3=0\), we get \(1-2s=s(1+s^2)\), hence this base is

\[
\frac{1+s^2}{s^3(1+s^2)}=s^{-3}=q^3.
\]

The phase has a unique maximum at \((0,0)\), and its quadratic expansion is

\[
\log\left(
\frac{1+s^2e^{i(\theta+\phi)}}{s^2e^{i(\theta+\phi)}(1-se^{i\theta}-se^{i\phi})}
\right)
=
3\log q-\frac{1}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}\theta&\phi\end{pmatrix}
A
\begin{pmatrix}\theta\\ \phi\end{pmatrix}
+O(|\theta,\phi|^3),
\]

where

\[
A=\frac{1}{1+s^2}
\begin{pmatrix}
2&1\\
1&2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\det A=\frac{3}{(1+s^2)^2},
\qquad
\sqrt{\det A}=\frac{\sqrt3}{1+s^2}.
\]

Also the prefactor at the saddle is

\[
\frac1{1-2s}=\frac1{s(1+s^2)}.
\]

The two-dimensional Gaussian asymptotic gives

\[
a_n\sim q^{3n}\cdot
\frac{1}{2\pi n}
\cdot
\frac{1}{1-2s}
\cdot
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\det A}}.
\]

Substituting the values above,

\[
a_n\sim q^{3n}\cdot
\frac1{2\pi n}
\cdot
\frac1{s(1+s^2)}
\cdot
\frac{1+s^2}{\sqrt3}
=
q^{3n}\cdot \frac{1}{n}\cdot \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt3\,s}.
\]

Since \(s=1/q\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{na_n}{q^{3n}}
=
\frac{q}{2\pi\sqrt3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{q}{2\pi\sqrt3}}
\]
